report.incident_title: Search slow and returning partial results since ~13:20
report.summary: Search latency and partial results are caused by a cold pricing cache after a pricing-cache primary hardware failure and failover at 13:17-13:18 UTC. The promoted replica held 0.4M keys versus 9.8M on the failed primary. Pricing-svc cache hit ratio fell from ~0.97 to ~0.15. Cache misses sent quote lookups to rates-db, which saturated (CPU ~96%). Pricing getQuotes calls then hit timeouts, search-api hit its 2500ms deadline, and ranking returned partial results (12 of 40 candidates). The 4.2.0 ranking code is not the bottleneck: its ranking span is ~33-36ms and warm-cache requests on 4.2.0 complete in ~236ms. Recommendation: do NOT roll back 4.2.0 as the fix. Run the pricing-warmer job now and reduce load on rates-db. The 4.2.0 deploy and the failover happened within minutes of each other, so the timing correlation is real but the mechanism points to the cache.
report.root_cause: pricing-cache-001 (primary) failed on host hardware fault at 13:17:42Z. ElastiCache promoted pricing-cache-002, which had only 0.4M keys versus 9.8M on the old primary (its replica had gone into a full resync at 13:02 after its replication backlog was exceeded). The resulting cold cache (hit ratio ~0.15) pushed most quote lookups to rates-db, which saturated. Pricing quote timeouts then exceeded search-api's 2500ms deadline, producing high p99 latency, errors and partial ranking. The warmer step that the runbook prescribes after a failover was not run.

hypotheses.statement: Cold pricing cache after the pricing-cache primary failover (promoted replica had 0.4M of 9.8M keys) drove cache misses onto rates-db, which saturated and caused pricing timeouts, search deadline overruns and partial ranking.

facts.text: pricing-cache-001 failed health checks (host hardware fault); pricing-cache-002 promoted at 13:18:31 with 0.4M keys vs 9.8M on the previous primary; replica-002 had gone into a full resync at 13:02:14.
pricing-svc cache_hit_ratio fell from ~0.96-0.97 (12:30-13:15) to 0.15 at 13:20 and was still only 0.52 at 14:25 (slowly refilling).
rates-db CPU rose from ~30% to 96% at 13:20 and was still 88% at 14:25.
pricing-svc WARN at 13:21:12: 'cache miss ratio 0.85 over last 60s; serving from rates-db'.
Slow trace t-c14-slow-1: pricing-svc getQuotes 2460ms with cache=miss, error=timeout; rates-db SELECT rate_quotes 2130ms; search-api deadline_exceeded at 2511ms.
rates-db WARN: SELECT rate_quotes took 2140ms at 13:26:41.
Latency p99 went from ~300ms (13:15) to 2610ms (13:20) and error rate from 0.3% to 5.1% at the same timestamp.
Runbook: rates-db can serve roughly a 20% miss ratio; after a cache flush or failover run pricing-warmer (about 15 minutes) to preload the top 50k hotels.
Past incident PIR-2026-021 (2026-04-02): slow search after pricing cache restarted empty; cold cache saturated rates-db; fixed by running pricing-warmer.
No pricing-warmer run appears in the logs or scheduled-job changes.

assumptions: The 0.4M vs 9.8M key counts reflect the actual data loss, not a reporting artifact.
rates-db's CPU and latency would recover if misses fell back to baseline (inferred from the 4.2.0 warm-cache trace and the runbook).

hypotheses.statement: The search-api 4.2.0 deploy (ltr-v7 model and feature-store client 2.9 to 3.1) caused the slowdown, as the reporter suspects.

facts.text: Ranking span (ranking.score, ltr-v7) takes 33-36ms in slow and fast traces. The slow time is spent in pricing-svc getQuotes, not ranking.
A 4.2.0 trace after recovery (14:12) with a cache hit completes in 236ms, with getQuotes at 16ms, so 4.2.0 is healthy when the cache is warm.
Baseline 4.1.3 trace (13:05) also fans out 40 quotes, so the fan-out is not new.
Timing: the 4.2.0 rollout finished at 13:16:40, but the cache hit ratio fell at 13:20 and the failover completed at 13:18:31, which matches the observed onset better than the deploy itself.
Metrics show search-api CPU fell from ~46% to ~39% at 13:20, and request rate was flat at ~850-860 rps, so the new code is not consuming more resources.

assumptions: The feature-store client has no metrics or logs in this data set, so a 3.1-specific feature-store regression can't be fully excluded. Its spans are absent from the traces, and the ranking span is fast.

hypotheses.statement: rates-db is independently degraded (for example a query-plan or lock problem), and the cache failover is only a coincident trigger.

facts.text: rates-db CPU stayed at 28-32% until 13:15 and rose only at 13:20, the same time the cache hit ratio collapsed. The slow statement is the cache-miss path query.

assumptions: Not tested. No rates-db query-plan, lock or replication data was retrieved.

corrective_actions.action: Run the pricing-warmer job now to preload quotes for the top ~50k hotels (about 15 minutes), per runbook rb-pricing-cache. Then watch pricing-svc cache_hit_ratio return toward 0.95+, rates-db CPU fall back toward 30%, and search p99 return toward 300ms.
corrective_actions.rationale: Directly fixes the cold-cache cause. Past incident PIR-2026-021 was resolved the same way. Organic refill is only +3 points every 5 minutes (0.15 to 0.52 over an hour), so waiting would take hours (extrapolation, an assumption).

corrective_actions.action: Reduce load on rates-db while the cache warms: throttle or shed cache-miss quote lookups, or cap per-request quote fan-out for ranking, so that search returns partial-but-fast results rather than deadline overruns. Coordinate with the search team on which ranking candidates to drop.
corrective_actions.rationale: rates-db at 96% CPU with 2.1s queries is the bottleneck. Limiting misses protects the database and the shared deals path (it is a dependency of web-frontend via deals-api, which I did not investigate).

corrective_actions.action: Do NOT roll back search-api 4.2.0 as the primary fix. Rollback would not restore the lost cache keys and would not stop the cold-cache misses. Revisit only if ranking span latency rises after the cache is warm (i.e., if 4.2.0 is actually slow under warm-cache conditions).
corrective_actions.rationale: Evidence shows the ranking code is fast (33-36ms), and warm-cache 4.2.0 requests take 236ms. A rollback adds deploy churn and reverts the ranking improvement without fixing the cause.

corrective_actions.action: Investigate why the pricing-cache replica needed a full resync at 13:02 (replication backlog exceeded) and why the promoted replica held only 0.4M of 9.8M keys. Check replica sizing, replication backlog settings, and whether the replacement pricing-cache-003 is fully synced before it is promoted in future.
corrective_actions.rationale: The data loss is what converted a hardware failure into a 40+ minute search outage. The data-loss mechanism is not yet explained.

corrective_actions.action: Automate the warmer as a post-failover and post-flush step (for example, trigger pricing-warmer on ElastiCache FailoverComplete events), and add it to the runbook as a required step with an owner.
corrective_actions.rationale: The runbook and PIR-2026-021 both specified this step, yet it was not run after this failover, so a manual step is too easy to miss.

corrective_actions.action: Add metrics and logs for pricing-cache (hit ratio, key count, replica lag, evictions, resync events) and alert on cache_hit_ratio drops and on key-count drops at failover. Currently pricing-cache returns no metrics or logs and feature-store returns no metrics, so this incident had to be inferred from pricing-svc and infra events.
corrective_actions.rationale: The pricing-cache data gap delayed diagnosis. An alert on hit ratio would have fired at 13:20 (the alert set only includes p99 and rates-db CPU).

missing_data: pricing-cache metrics and logs: queries returned empty (call-0006, call-0009), so the key count, hit/miss breakdown, replica lag and evictions are only inferred from pricing-svc and ElastiCache events.
feature-store metrics and logs (call-0008): none available, so a 3.1 client regression can't be fully excluded from metrics alone, although the ranking spans are fast.
Why replica pricing-cache-002 full-resynced at 13:02 and whether its resync completed before promotion.
rates-db query-plan, lock and replication data for the rate_quotes queries (no data retrieved).
Whether the warmer job, if run, would finish before the deadline overruns end; whether deals-api (web-frontend dependency) is also affected by rates-db saturation.
vendor status report (call-0022) was not available.

questions_for_human: Should we run pricing-warmer now? It takes about 15 minutes, and the expected effect (a return to baseline latency) rests on the runbook and past incident, not on a measured run here.
Is there a way to shed or cap cache-miss quote fan-out on rates-db temporarily? The search team and pricing team should decide which candidates to drop.
Did the search team or anyone else touch pricing-cache, ElastiCache or the warmer schedule around 13:00-13:20? No such change appears in get_changes.
